(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] | highlights = * [[NBA champion]] ({{nbafy|2020}}) * [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] ([[2025–26 EuroLeague|2026]]) * [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Super League]] champion ([[2025-26 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2026]]) * [[Turkish Basketball Cup|Turkish Cup]] winner ([[2026 Turkish Basketball Cup|2026]]) * [[Turkish Basketball Super Cup|Turkish Super Cup]] winner ([[2025 Turkish Basketball Presidential Cup|2025]]) * [[Big 12]] All-Freshman Team ([[2018–19 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|2019]]) }} '''Talen Jalee Horton-Tucker''' ({{IPAc-en|'|t|eɪ|l|ə|n}}; born November 25, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. Horton-Tucker played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==Early life== Born in Chicago, Horton–Tucker was raised in [[Uptown, Chicago|Uptown]], a neighborhood of Chicago. Horton–Tucker is the son of Shirley Horton and Marlin Tucker.{{cite web |title=Talen-Horton Tucker Bio |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/talen-horton-tucker/9932 |website=Iowa State Cyclones |access-date=8 November 2019}} For elementary school, Horton–Tucker attended St. Matthias Elementary School in Chicago, where he had his No. 5 jersey [[retired number|retired]]. Horton–Tucker played at [[Simeon Career Academy]] where he helped the Wolverines to three straight City Championships.{{Cite news |last=O'Brien |first=Michael |date=2018-02-18 |title=Simeon beats Orr for third straight city championship |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/simeon-beats-orr-for-third-straight-city-championship/ |access-date=2019-01-18 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |language=en}} A four-star recruit in [[ESPN]]'s ranking,{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/230690/talen-horton-tucker|title=Talen Horton-Tucker - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2019-01-18}} he committed to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] in October 2017, choosing the Cyclones over schools such as [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/Article/BREAKING-Iowa-State-lands-commitment-from-4-star-Chicago-guard-Talen-Horton-Tucker-109492093/|title=Iowa State lands Chicago prospect Talen Horton-Tucker|work=247Sports.com|access-date=2019-01-18}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Talen Horton-Tucker | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Chicago|Chicago, IL]] | highschool = [[Simeon Career Academy|Simeon]] (IL) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 220 | 40 = | commitdate = October 26, 2017 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 85 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Iowa State 2018 Basketball Commitments | espn ref title = 2018 Iowa State Cyclones Recruiting Class | rivals school = iowastate | espn schoolid = 66 | rivals overall = 33 | 247 overall = 65 | espn overall = 66 | accessdate = January 17, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 20, 2018, Horton–Tucker scored a career-high 26 points and grabbed a career-high 14 rebounds in a win against [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{cite news |title=Illini haunted by ex-recruit vs. Iowa State |url=https://qconline.com/sports/college_sports/illini-haunted-by-ex-recruit-vs-iowa-state/article_2bf9a41c-9d26-5a37-ad4d-19eca2062db6.html |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=[[Rock Island Dispatch-Argus]] |date=November 20, 2018}} As a freshman, Horton–Tucker averaged 11.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 27 minutes per game. Horton–Tucker declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] after his freshman season.{{cite news|last=Givony|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26417903/iowa-state-horton-tucker-declares-draft|title=Iowa State's Horton-Tucker declares for draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 1, 2019|access-date=July 2, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2022)=== On June 20, 2019, Horton-Tucker was selected as the 46th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]]. He was traded on draft night to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for a 2020 second round draft pick and cash considerations.{{cite web|title=Lakers Acquire Talen Horton-Tucker|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/draft19-acquire-horton-tucker|date=June 20, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 20, 2019}} On July 13, Horton-Tucker signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakes Sign Talen Horton-Tucker|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190713-lakers-sign-horton-tucker|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 14, 2019|date=July 13, 2019}} He was assigned to the Lakers’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[South Bay Lakers]], for the opening of the G League season.{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2019 |title=South Bay Lakers Set Opening Night Roster |url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |access-date=November 7, 2019 |website=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=January 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121012818/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |url-status=dead }} He made his NBA debut on December 8, against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web|title=Timberwolves vs. Lakers - Box Score - December 8, 2019 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401160984|access-date=2020-08-15|website=ESPN.com}} He received a larger role during the [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA Bubble]] as the Lakers had clinched the best record in the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] and even started in the regular season finale.{{Cite web|title=Talen Horton-Tucker 2019-20 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hortota01/gamelog/2020/|access-date=2020-08-15|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} On September 12, 2020, Horton-Tucker scored 9 points in 10 minutes off the bench in Game 5 of Western Conference semifinals, helping the Lakers secure a 119–96 victory against the [[Houston Rockets]] and advance into the next round. Horton-Tucker won an NBA championship when the Lakers defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2020 NBA Finals]] in 6 games. He became the second-youngest player in NBA history to win a championship, at 19 years and 322 days.{{cite news|title=The youngest players to win an NBA title |date=January 4, 2021|url=https://hoopshype.com/gallery/youngest-players-nba-title-champions/ |website=hoopshype.com |access-date=2021-10-20}} After a strong preseason, Horton-Tucker became a regular rotational player in the 2020–21 regular season.{{cite news|title=Lakers' Talen Horton-Tucker: In regular rotation|date=January 4, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-talen-horton-tucker-in-regular-rotation/|access-date=January 11, 2021}}{{cite news|first=Jovan|last=Buha|title='We're a work in progress': Lakers continue to experiment with rotation|date=January 9, 2021|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2311895/2021/01/09/lakers-rotation-wesley-matthews-bulls/|url-access=subscription|access-date=January 11, 2021|quote="Through the first 10 games, we’ve played B, B-plus basketball," James said. "And that’s absolutely OK because we are a team that added basically five new pieces to the rotation in Trezz, Dennis, Marc, Wes and also Talen (Horton-Tucker). We’ve added five new pieces to our regular rotation, and we’re still learning each other.}} On January 10, 2021, he scored a career-high 17 points off the bench in the team's 120–102 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |title=Lakers vs. Rockets - Box Score - January 10, 2021 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401267306 |access-date=2021-07-14 |website=ESPN.com}} On
